key_insight: Machine learning can support computer algebra by guiding costly algorithmic decisions or performing symbolic computations directly.
engineering_relevance: ML-guided heuristics and algorithm selection may reduce symbolic computation costs, potentially expanding the practical use of mathematically rigorous methods.
method: Systematically review ML applications in computer algebra.
Cover cylindrical algebraic decomposition, Gröbner bases, symbolic integration, and other tasks.
Compare approaches ranging from decision trees to transformers.
evidence_signal: The survey identifies a lack of benchmark datasets, limiting reliable comparisons between methods and assessment of model generalizability.
watch_item: ML outputs and heuristic choices require careful validation; explainable AI may improve trust but does not establish mathematical correctness.
paper_title: A Survey on the Use of Machine Learning within Computer Algebra
